purpose: MeasurementWithSpheres is a 3D Slicer scripted module that fits four spheres (via 3-point circumcircles) to 12 markup fiducial points and creates markup lines and angles between the sphere centers to measure distances and angles. It also provides helper controls to generate and delete markup lines at specified coordinates.
summary:
Reviewed `MeasurementWithSpheres` at commit `a867ce7e96984a11fdcedec0eed5704ddd16a7a8` (PR #2047). The extension is licensed under Apache-2.0, has a valid catalog entry and CMake build configuration, and contains no malicious behavior or data transmission. However, `MeasurementWithSpheresParameterNode` calls `slicer.mrmlScene.AddNewNodeByClass(...)` at class definition time (lines 74-79), which adds four markup nodes (`Length1`, `Length2`, `Length3`, `Angle`) to the user's scene at Slicer startup whenever the module is imported, even if the user never opens the module, and breaks `@parameterNodeWrapper`.

🔴 Do not merge yet: `MeasurementWithSpheres.py` modifies `slicer.mrmlScene` at module import / Slicer startup (lines 74-81).

safety.rationale: Inspected all files in commit `a867ce7e96984a11fdcedec0eed5704ddd16a7a8`. There are no network requests, subprocess calls, file deletions, dynamic code execution, or unsafe deserialization.

environment.rationale: Inspected `MeasurementWithSpheres/MeasurementWithSpheres.py`. No packages are installed, but `MeasurementWithSpheresParameterNode` calls `slicer.mrmlScene.AddNewNodeByClass(...)` four times inside the class definition body (lines 74-79), which executes at module import during Slicer startup and pollutes `slicer.mrmlScene` for all users even when the module is never opened.

packaging.rationale: Inspected the catalog entry, `CMakeLists.txt`, and `MeasurementWithSpheres/CMakeLists.txt`. All required scripts and UI/icon resources exist and are installed by CMake, and dependencies match. A `.pyc` file in `__pycache__` is tracked and `CMakeLists.txt` has placeholder icon/screenshot URLs, which are minor/info cleanup items.

license.rationale: Inspected `LICENSE`, which provides the standard Apache License 2.0 text permitting use, modification, and redistribution. No third-party code or restricted weights are bundled.

soundness.rationale: Inspected `MeasurementWithSpheres/MeasurementWithSpheres.py` and `MeasurementWithSpheres/Resources/UI/MeasurementWithSpheres.ui`. The `@parameterNodeWrapper` class contains untyped attributes and `vtk.vtkSphereSource` instances that are incompatible with `parameterNodeWrapper`, and `createAngle` assumes a fiducial node with at least 12 points already exists in the scene without validation.

utility.rationale: Inspected `README.md` and `MeasurementWithSpheres/MeasurementWithSpheres.py`. The README illustrates the workflow with screenshots, though the module lacks automated tests (and `MeasurementWithSpheresTest` is empty) and appears to be an early prototype/example module.

findings.title: MRML nodes are added to the scene at module import (Slicer startup) and break @parameterNodeWrapper
findings.evidence:
@parameterNodeWrapper
class MeasurementWithSpheresParameterNode:
...
    lineNode = slicer.mrmlScene.AddNewNodeByClass('vtkMRMLMarkupsLineNode', 'Length1')
  
    observerId:int
    lineNode2 =  slicer.mrmlScene.AddNewNodeByClass('vtkMRMLMarkupsLineNode', 'Length2')
    lineNode3 =  slicer.mrmlScene.AddNewNodeByClass('vtkMRMLMarkupsLineNode', 'Length3')
    angleNode = slicer.mrmlScene.AddNewNodeByClass('vtkMRMLMarkupsAngleNode','Angle')
findings.explanation: When Slicer starts up and imports `MeasurementWithSpheres.py`, the class body of `MeasurementWithSpheresParameterNode` executes immediately and adds four markup nodes (`Length1`, `Length2`, `Length3`, `Angle`) to `slicer.mrmlScene` even if the user never opens the module. Furthermore, `@parameterNodeWrapper` fails when `MeasurementWithSpheresLogic.getParameterNode()` is called because attributes without type annotations (`lineNode`, `lineNode2`, `lineNode3`, `angleNode`, `markups`, `spheres`, `i`, `count`) or with unsupported types (`vtk.vtkSphereSource`) cannot be wrapped by Slicer's parameterNodeWrapper.
findings.suggestion: Do not call `slicer.mrmlScene.AddNewNodeByClass` at class definition time (module import). Instead, declare typed node fields on the `@parameterNodeWrapper` class (e.g., `lineNode: slicer.vtkMRMLMarkupsLineNode`) and create the nodes only when the user opens or runs the module. Keep non-MRML runtime objects such as `vtk.vtkSphereSource` instances on the Widget or Logic instance rather than in the `@parameterNodeWrapper` class.

findings.title: Missing validation for markups node existence and required number of control points
findings.evidence:
center0, radius0 = self.logic.sphereFrom3Points(self._parameterNode.markups,0)
        center1, radius1 = self.logic.sphereFrom3Points(self._parameterNode.markups, 3)
        center2, radius2 = self.logic.sphereFrom3Points(self._parameterNode.markups, 6)
        center3, radius3 = self.logic.sphereFrom3Points(self._parameterNode.markups, 9)
findings.explanation: `createAngle` and `sphereFrom3Points` assume that a `vtkMRMLMarkupsFiducialNode` exists in the scene and has at least 12 control points, without checking. If no fiducial node exists, `markupsNode` is `None` and calling `GetNthControlPointPosition` raises an `AttributeError`. If fewer than 12 points exist, `GetNthControlPointPosition` leaves the points at `(0, 0, 0)`, resulting in division by zero in `sphereFrom3Points`. Also note that `sphereFrom3Points` computes the circumcircle in the plane of 3 points rather than a 4-point 3D sphere.
findings.suggestion: Add a `qMRMLNodeComboBox` to let the user select the input `vtkMRMLMarkupsFiducialNode`, and check that the node exists and has at least 12 non-collinear control points before computing spheres, showing an informative error message if not.

findings.title: VTK observer callback signature and cleanup mismatch
findings.explanation: `self.changePoints` is registered directly as a VTK observer callback (`AddObserver(slicer.vtkMRMLMarkupsNode.PointModifiedEvent, self.changePoints, 2)`). VTK passes `(caller, event)` to observer callbacks, which bind to `markups` and `spheres`, while removing the observer in `resetView` occurs after `self._parameterNode.markups` is already removed from the scene (`AttributeError` if `markups` was `None`).
findings.suggestion: Define the observer callback with signature `def changePoints(self, caller=None, event=None) -> None:` and use `VTKObservationMixin` (`self.addObserver` / `self.removeObserver`) so observers are automatically cleaned up.

findings.title: Template placeholder URLs/contributors in CMakeLists.txt and committed __pycache__ bytecode
findings.evidence:
set(EXTENSION_CONTRIBUTORS "John Doe (AnyWare Corp.), Cagatay Alptekin (Non-Nocere)")
set(EXTENSION_DESCRIPTION "This is an example of a simple extension that creates spheres and calculate length angles at different positions.")
set(EXTENSION_ICONURL "https://www.example.com/Slicer/Extensions/MeasurementWithSpheres.png")
set(EXTENSION_SCREENSHOTURLS "https://www.example.com/Slicer/Extensions/MeasurementWithSpheres/Screenshots/1.png")
findings.explanation: `CMakeLists.txt` still contains template placeholder metadata (`John Doe (AnyWare Corp.)`, `www.example.com` icon and screenshot URLs), and the repository tracks a compiled bytecode file `MeasurementWithSpheres/__pycache__/MeasurementWithSpheres.cpython-39.pyc`.
findings.suggestion: Update `EXTENSION_ICONURL`, `EXTENSION_SCREENSHOTURLS`, `EXTENSION_CONTRIBUTORS`, and `EXTENSION_CATEGORY` in `CMakeLists.txt` to point to the repository's actual icon (`MeasurementWithSpheres.png`) and screenshots, and remove `MeasurementWithSpheres/__pycache__/` from git tracking.

not_checked: Runtime execution inside 3D Slicer (no shell or Slicer environment available in review container)
questions_for_author: Did you intend to fit spheres from 3 points (circumcircle in the plane of 3 points) or 4 points in 3D space?
